title: Sign test
biology: Behavioral biologists record the change in refuge-use time after a predator cue.
design: Each independent fish is measured twice; the changes are skewed.
data_characteristics: One continuous response or paired differences
question: Is an increase just as likely as a decrease in refuge-use time?
null: Among nonzero changes, positive and negative changes are equally likely; for continuous differences, the median is zero.
options: Drop and report exact zero differences
binom.test tests the number of positive changes
assumptions: Median interpretation assumes a continuous distribution
parametric: A paired t test answers a mean-change question
Model skew explicitly if the mean is the target
nonparametric: Signed-rank adds magnitude information but needs symmetry
practice: If a few fish change by a very large amount, does that affect the sign test statistic?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1104)
change <- rgamma(30, shape = 1.4, scale = 5) - 3
d <- data.frame(fish = 1:30, change_seconds = round(change, 1))
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
values <- sort(d$change_seconds)
cols <- ifelse(values > 0, "#246A73", "#B7663E")
plot(seq_along(values), values, type = "n", xlab = "Fish ordered by change",
     ylab = "Change in refuge-use time (seconds)")
abline(h = 0, col = "gray55", lty = 2)
segments(seq_along(values), 0, seq_along(values), values, col = cols, lwd = 2)
points(seq_along(values), values, pch = 19, col = cols)
code_analysis:
nonzero <- d$change_seconds[d$change_seconds != 0]
positive <- sum(nonzero > 0)
fit <- binom.test(positive, length(nonzero), p = .5,
                 alternative = "two.sided")
generating_model: 30 independent changes are Gamma(shape 1.4, scale 5) minus 3 seconds, rounded to 0.1 seconds. Exact zeros, if present, are excluded from the sign comparison.
generating_truth: Positive changes are more likely than negative changes. The unrounded mean is 4 seconds, but the sign test is about direction rather than that mean.
teaching_point: A sign test handles asymmetric differences by asking about the probability of a positive change.
